title: Routing policy interpreter overhaul for multi-region, tier, and fallback variants
creator: Ava Chen
description: Background: Current routing policy DSL has grown organically to cover region affinity, customer tier routing, and model-fallback rules. Over time we've accumulated special-cased precedence logic and silent fallbacks which make validation, predictable behavior, and testing difficult. This ticket is to refactor the policy interpreter and the config schema so that routing rules are declarative, deterministic, and can be statically validated.
goals: 1) Define a single canonical routing rule AST that expresses region selection, tier routing, and fallback chains; 2) Implement a JSON/YAML schema and validator with clear ergonomics and helpful error messages; 3) Ensure backward-compatible migration path for existing policy configs with a migration lint tool; 4) Add unit, integration, and e2e tests; 5) Rollout as a canary behind a feature flag and provide observability for mismatches and fallback rates.
acceptance_criteria:
- New canonical DSL schema accepted by policy-engine and passes validation for all existing test configs (using migration linter).
- Deterministic precedence defined and documented: explicit route -> tier-specific route -> region affinity -> global fallback.
- Policy validator surface exposes clear error messages with line/field locations.
- Runtime chooseRoute(policy, requestMeta) produces identical results to the legacy engine for 95% of production traces (we'll investigate divergences).
- A migration linter PR is available and documented for customers/operators to preview config changes.
- Canary rollout metrics: fallback invocation rate and increased latency at canary < 1% relative to baseline.
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Strict schema may break poorly formed older policies; mitigated via a migration linter and 'compat' mode.
- Making precedence fully deterministic simplifies reasoning but can remove some implicit optimistic fallbacks; will add opt-in fallback escalation policies.
- Validator complexity increases upfront engineering cost but provides long-term operability improvements.
implementation_notes:
- Introduce a canonical AST module under runtime/policy/ast.
- Add a policy-validator CLI (policyctl validate <file>) that emits structured diagnostics.
- Implement a migration mode: legacy-compat-suggester that rewrites deprecated constructs to canonical form.
- Add policy_interpreter_v2 feature flag and route resolution telemetry (policy_id, request_hash, chosen_variant, reason_code).
- Tests: unit for AST transforms, property tests comparing legacy vs v2 on recorded traces, integration tests in staging with canary traffic.
testing_plan:
- Create a corpus of 10k sampled routing traces (region, tier, model variant sequences) from prod (anonymized).
- Run diff tool to compare decisions between legacy and new interpreter.
- Add fuzz tests for malformed configs to exercise validator messages.
- Staging canary: 5% traffic for 48h, then 25% for 24h conditioned on metrics.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag. 2) Deploy to staging, run migration linter across corpora. 3) Enable for internal beta customers and run canary with 5% traffic. 4) Monitor fallback rate, latency, error rates for 72h. 5) Gradual ramp to 100% if metrics stable. 6) Publish migration guide and opt-in compat flags for customers.

security_considerations: Policy files may reference customer-specific model IDs and region constraints. Validator must not leak model or customer IDs in error logs to telemetry; errors should be hashed or redacted when sent to central telemetry. KMS access not required for validation but ensure any config artifacts stored in S3 follow existing encryption-at-rest policies.
